newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks to rise on foreign ceiling expansion.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks to rise on foreign ceiling expansion.

text.p: Anticipation of an inflow of foreign funds in line with an expanding foreign stock ownership limit would continue to boost Seoul stocks on Tuesday, brokers said.
They said a decision by banks to extend 80.4 billion won in emergency loans to the financially troubled Jinro Group would also contribute to the market's upbeat mood.
"Follow-through buying is expected to last in blue chips," said Lee Hee-myung of Samsung Securities.
The composite stock index closed on Monday at 704.16, up 4.40 points.
South Korea will raise the foreign stock holding ceiling to 23 percent from Friday, compared with 20 percent at present.

The Jinro bailout is aimed at six major Jinro affiliates. But loans would be granted only after the group chairman issues a letter allowing banks to dispose of his faimily's shareholding in group affiliates.
"The aid package was less than expected. But it would help soothe worries about instability in the money market," Lee said.
